signs: Water overflowing the gutter edge during rainfall (clog or undersized system), per Angi
Gutters sagging or pulling away from the fascia (failed hangers or a rotted mounting board), per Angi
Peeling paint, soft spots, or stains on the fascia and soffit (prolonged overflow soaking the boards), per Angi
Water pooling against the foundation or basement seepage after rain (downspout discharge too close to the building), per Angi
Visible joint leaks, rust streaks, or separated seams (a sectional gutter failing at the lapped joints), per Englert
Standing water in the gutter trough after rain stops (lost pitch or settled hangers), per American Gutter Masters / Vermont Gutter Co.
Thick ice ridges and large icicles at the eaves in winter (an ice dam backing meltwater at the roof edge, driven by attic heat escape, not the gutter), per University of Minnesota Extension

technicalFacts.fact: A clogged gutter overflows and saturates the fascia and soffit and sheds water against the foundation, driving basement seepage and hydrostatic pressure
Standard residential gutter is a 5-inch K-style; a 6-inch K-style holds roughly 50% more water (5-in ~1.2 gal/ft, 6-in ~2.0 gal/ft), used on large/steep roofs and high-rainfall exposures
Downspout outlet is matched to gutter size: a 5-inch K-style gutter pairs with a 2-by-3 downspout, a 6-inch gutter with a 3-by-4 downspout
Seamless gutters are formed on site as one continuous piece, eliminating the lapped joints where sectional gutters most often leak under debris load and thermal cycling
Industry-standard gutter drainage slope is roughly 1/4 inch per 10 feet (range 1/4 to 1/2 inch) toward the outlet — a trade rule, NOT a code requirement
technicalFacts.source: American Gutter Masters / Vermont Gutter Co.

technicalFacts.fact: A full gutter (water plus wet debris) can weigh ~20 lb/ft, rising to 60-plus lb/ft with ice/snow — enough to pull gutters off the fascia if hangers are spaced too far apart
Hidden hanger spacing is ~24 in standard, tightening to ~18 in in snow/ice climates
technicalFacts.source: Art of Gutter / Maine Gutter Works

technicalFacts.fact: Downspout extensions should discharge at least 4 to 6 feet from the foundation to route runoff away from the basement
Gutters need cleaning twice per year (spring and fall), rising to 3 to 4 times per year on a property surrounded by pine trees
Ice dams are caused by attic heat escape that melts the snowpack and refreezes meltwater at the cold eave; gutters only aggravate eave backup and do not cause ice dams
technicalFacts.source: University of Minnesota Extension / Building Science Digest 135

technicalFacts.fact: Repair a gutter when damage is localized to a seam, hanger, or section on a system inside its service life; replace when corrosion, sagging, or leaks recur across the run
technicalFacts.source: InterNACHI Estimated Life Expectancy Chart / Englert

codes.requirement: Ice barrier installed from the eave to at least 24 inches inside the exterior wall line (at least 36 inches up-slope on roofs 8:12 or steeper); protects the ice-dam-prone roof edge where gutters meet the eave. NJ-adopted via N.J.A.C. 5:23 (2021 IRC).
Self-adhering polymer-modified bitumen ice-and-water membrane that self-seals around fasteners (the eave ice-barrier material).

defabToKill.issue: Invented ice-load specifics presented as fact: 'a single foot of 6-inch gutter filled with ice weighs 18+ pounds, and a 30-foot run accumulates over 500 pounds.'
defabToKill.fix: Use the sourced approximation: a full gutter weighs ~20 lb/ft, rising to 60+ lb/ft with ice/snow, enough to pull gutters off the fascia if hangers are spaced too far apart, per Green Sun NJ. Do not assert precise 18 lb/ft or 500 lb totals.

defabToKill.issue: Unsourced NJ rainfall climate claims used as load justification: 'NJ receives 46-50 inches of rainfall annually,' '1-2 inches per hour during summer thunderstorms.'
defabToKill.fix: Drop the invented precise rainfall figures; ground sizing in the gutter-capacity facts (5-in vs 6-in ~50% more water) per Storm Master / My Gutter Doctor, and overflow consequences per Angi.

defabToKill.issue: Unsourced 'clay-heavy soils' and '10x cost' / 'thousands of gallons per year' foundation-damage claims dramatize without a named source.
defabToKill.fix: Replace with the grounded mechanism: a clogged or overflowing gutter saturates fascia and soffit and sheds water against the foundation, driving basement seepage, per Angi; downspouts should discharge 4-6 ft from the foundation, per Boggs Inspection.

defabToKill.issue: Installation prices contradict the gold/HomeGuide: '$8 to $15 per linear foot' for seamless aluminum and an invented whole-home total '$1,200 to $3,000' for a 'typical NJ home with 150-200 feet' — no named aggregator source.
defabToKill.fix: Use HomeGuide: gutter installation $12-$25/linear ft installed; by material vinyl $8-$12, aluminum $10-$20, steel $10-$35, copper $35-$45/ft. Do NOT publish a self-attributed whole-project total; use per-foot pricing plus NQR free-written-estimate framing.

defabToKill.issue: Fabricated repair sub-prices not matching the gold: 'sagging section $100-250,' 'leaking seams $75-200 per joint,' 'downspout $100-300,' 'comprehensive visit $300-800,' 'cleaning $150-350 / $100-250.'
defabToKill.fix: Use HomeGuide per the gold: gutter repair $100-$450 (avg ~$275); sagging $75-$300; leak/seam reseal $100-$225. Cleaning cadence (not price) is twice/yr spring+fall, 3-4x with pine trees, per Angi/GAF — no invented cleaning dollar figures in the gold.

defabToKill.issue: Invented downstream-damage cost stack with no source: foundation repair '$8,000-15,000,' basement waterproofing '$5,000-12,000,' landscape '$1,000-5,000,' basement flooding '$10,000-30,000,' and 'copper lasts 50-70 years without maintenance.'
defabToKill.fix: Remove all unsourced damage-cost totals and the ROI framing. Copper lifespan is 50-plus years per the InterNACHI Estimated Life Expectancy Chart (not '50-70 without maintenance'). Keep the value story qualitative and source-grounded.

defabToKill.issue: Invented precision: 'reducing leak risk by 80% compared to sectional systems' and 'sectional gutters develop leaks at every joint within 5-10 years.'
defabToKill.fix: State qualitatively per Englert: seamless gutters run one continuous piece, eliminating the lapped joints where sectional gutters most often leak under debris load and thermal cycling. No invented 80% or 5-10 year figures.

defabToKill.issue: Fabricated sizing math: '5-inch K-style drains approximately 5,520 square feet per downspout,' '6-inch handle 40% more volume,' 'one downspout for every 40 feet... NJ building practice requires.'
defabToKill.fix: Use the sourced capacity: a 6-inch K-style holds roughly 50% more water than a 5-inch profile (5-in ~1.2 gal/ft, 6-in ~2.0 gal/ft), per Storm Master / My Gutter Doctor; match 5-in to a 2x3 downspout and 6-in to a 3x4 downspout. Drop the invented 5,520 sq ft, 40%, and 40-ft 'code/practice' claims.

defabToKill.issue: Slope and hanger specs stated as hard minimums/requirements: 'slope... 1/4 inch per 10 feet minimum,' 'hanger spacing every 24 inches maximum for NJ ice loads.'
defabToKill.fix: Frame 1/4 in per 10 ft as a trade drainage rule (not code), per American Gutter Masters / Vermont Gutter Co.; hanger spacing ~24 in standard, tightening to ~18 in in snow/ice climates, per Art of Gutter / Maine Gutter Works. Downspout discharge 4-6 ft from foundation, per Boggs Inspection.

articleAngles.signs: Definitively answer the seven concrete symptoms that mean a property needs gutter installation or repair — overflow during rain (clog/undersizing), sagging or pulling from the fascia (failed hangers/rotted board), peeling paint and soft fascia/soffit, foundation pooling or basement seepage, joint leaks and rust streaks on sectional runs, standing trough water (lost pitch), and eave ice ridges — each grounded in Angi (overflow/rot/seepage), Englert (sectional seam leaks), American Gutter Masters/Vermont Gutter Co. (pitch), and University of Minnesota Extension (ice dams = attic heat, not the gutter). Use the Green Sun NJ ~20/60+ lb/ft load fact for the sagging section, not invented per-foot ice weights.
articleAngles.costGuide: Answer with HomeGuide figures only: gutter installation runs roughly $12-$25 per linear foot installed (by material vinyl $8-$12, aluminum $10-$20, steel $10-$35, copper $35-$45/ft), and a gutter repair runs $100-$450 (average near $275), with sagging repair $75-$300 and leak/seam reseal $100-$225 — all per HomeGuide. State plainly there is no fixed whole-project total (cost scales with linear footage, material, and profile) and that NQR provides a free written estimate; tie material to lifespan via the InterNACHI chart (copper 50+ yr, aluminum 20-40+ yr, steel 20 yr, vinyl 25+ yr).
articleAngles.decision: Broad homeowner overview: how a gutter system protects the fascia, soffit, and foundation (Angi); when to repair vs replace (localized seam/hanger damage inside service life = repair; recurring corrosion/sagging/leaks = replace, per InterNACHI + Englert); seamless vs sectional (Englert — seamless eliminates lapped joints); sizing (5-in standard, 6-in holds ~50% more water; matched 2x3/3x4 downspouts, per Storm Master/My Gutter Doctor); the ~1/4 in per 10 ft trade slope rule and ~24-in (18-in in ice climates) hanger spacing; 4-6 ft downspout discharge (Boggs Inspection); twice-yearly cleaning, 3-4x with pines (Angi/GAF); and the eave ice barrier code point (IRC R905.1.2, 24 in inside the wall line) noting ice dams stem from attic heat, not gutters. Verify NQR is a registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor (never 'licensed').
